screen: #/model/transdigm/2025-06-30/forecast and the other five pages of the run (fixture copy with the run's forecast removed; error)
title: A run with no forecast cannot be shown at all: the reader rejects the whole run, so the Forecast page has no 'no forecast was published' state and the run's Front page, Analysis, Model, Portfolio fit and Limitations vanish with it.
expected: CM-067: on a run with no forecast (a lite run, a past short snapshot) the Forecast page states that no forecast was published. The library's own run tabs already expect such runs (web/src/pages/library/parts/RunFrame.tsx:105-108 draws 'No forecast for this run' when forecastHref is null). D-31: a designed state, not a lost page.
actual: web/src/pages/model/slice/read.ts:299-316 requires `forecast` (object), exactly two cases and every part. With `forecast` deleted from the run, #/model/runs lists the run as 'transdigm 2025-06-30 Could not be read' and every address of the run, including front, analysis, statements and limitations, draws 'This part of the library could not be read runs[0].forecast: missing'. A run with one case fails the same way ('expected two cases, the side by side chart draws two'). No page states that no forecast was published.
suggested_change: Make `forecast` optional in the reader and draw one fixed sentence on the Forecast page when it is absent, keeping the other five pages readable; allow fewer than two cases where there is no forecast.

screen: #/model/<issuer>/<run>/<any page> and #/model/runs (fixture copies with a part removed; error)
title: An unreadable run is explained to the reader with the reader's raw field path ('runs[1].front.headline: missing') and listed by its raw issuer slug and run id.
expected: D-31: errors are an alert or notice in plain words, 'no raw error string'; D-04: nothing looks extracted from a file. D-11 and the AGENTS.md voice standard: the reader is a portfolio manager.
actual: RunPage passes `unreadable.reason` straight into the notice description (RunPage.tsx:58) and RunsIndexPage draws the slug and run id of the entry ('transdigm', '2023-06-30', 'Could not be read'). With front.headline removed the page reads 'This part of the library could not be read runs[1].front.headline: missing'; with one case removed it reads 'runs[0].cases: expected two cases, the side by side chart draws two'. The Model's other runs stay readable, which is correct.
suggested_change: Draw one fixed plain sentence for an unreadable run on the reading pages and keep the path text for the analyst (for example behind a disclosure on the index or in the console).

title: Every link from the Model pages into a library run dead-ends in the fixture: all 89 such link instances on the six run pages (breadcrumb issuer, Back to the report, Evidence tab, 'See the 3 gaps in Evidence', Forecast's Overview, Changes and Modules tabs and every trace control) open 'No such issuer', and all trace controls share one Evidence address.
expected: README Scope: the static app opens from disk on web/public/data.js fixtures. CM-008, CM-009 and CT-047: a trace control leads to the item's basis in Evidence; CM-031: the run label names a run the library holds. web/fixtures/library.json holds halden-aerostructures, corvane-packaging, tessaly-foods, ardenne-cable, lumora-health, corvane-fasteners and brevane-marine.
actual: web/fixtures/model.json holds one run, transdigm 2025-06-30, whose links are #/library/transdigm/2025-06-30/overview, .../evidence, .../changes and .../modules. The library fixture has no transdigm, so each of the 12 report links, the 75 evidence links (the Evidence tab, the gaps link and the trace controls) and the changes and modules links opens a page reading 'No such issuer. The library holds no issuer at this address.' The 'Show the sources for X' controls among them all carry the single address #/library/transdigm/2025-06-30/evidence, so even with a matching issuer they would not reach the item. The Library link (#/) works. The static app therefore cannot show a reader the path from a Model figure to its source.
suggested_change: Give the model fixture a run the library fixture holds (or add the run to library.json) and give each trace an item address of the form #/library/<issuer>/<run>/evidence/trace/<item>.

screen: Any trace control on #/model/.../statements (full); same control on every Model page
title: A trace control on the Model pages is a plain link that leaves the Model for the Evidence page: it opens no drawer, and Back returns a reset page (case choice, scroll position and focus lost).
expected: CM-008: a figure opens the trace drawer, which lists the Basis items. CM-009 and CT-047: focus returns to the opening control when the drawer closes. D-06 and D-38: Escape or Close return focus to the opener.
actual: web/src/pages/model/parts/TraceControl.tsx:25-26 is a react-aria Link with the slice's address. With Downside chosen and the page scrolled 1500 px, pressing Enter on 'Show the sources for Debt by instrument' navigates to #/library/transdigm/2025-06-30/evidence (no dialog opens, dialog count 0). Back returns to the Model with the Base case checked again, scrollTop 0 and document.activeElement BODY. The library's own pages use a drawer (S4 section).
suggested_change: Open the library's trace drawer from the Model's trace controls (or keep the link and restore case, scroll and focus on return); the owner decides which.

title: At 390 px the Statements table cannot be read: the sticky label column takes 224 of the table's 260 px, leaving a 36 px window for the figures.
expected: D-42: at narrow widths content reflows or a data table scrolls and stays readable; D-02: a statement is a table (R1). CM-064: the model grid is shown.
actual: StatementTable.tsx:122 sets `w-full min-w-[1100px] table-fixed` with 120 px period columns, so the label column is 1100 - 7 x 120 - 36 = 224 px and is sticky (lines 127 and 170). In a 260 px card the reader sees the labels and a 36 px slice of one figure column, for example 'EBITDA margin 5'. There is no card or list form of the statements for a narrow window and no Chart or Table toggle here.
suggested_change: Narrow the sticky label column below 640 px (for example 40 percent of the window, wrapping) or release the sticky column and let the whole table scroll.

title: At 390 px the Statements tab list is 445 px wide inside a 260 px card with overflow visible: 'Balance sheet' is cut by the card edge, 'Key measures' lies past the screen edge and the whole page scrolls sideways by 120 px.
expected: D-42: no two-direction scrolling for anything but data tables and charts; D-35: every tab reachable.
actual: The tab list (role tablist) has scrollWidth 445, clientWidth 260 and overflow-x visible; tab right edges are 194, 281, 397 and 510 px in a 390 px window, and main's scrollWidth is 510. The fourth statement is reachable by arrow keys or by scrolling the whole page; a pointer tap at the screen edge missed it. Nothing signals that a fourth tab exists.
suggested_change: Let the tab list scroll inside the card (overflow-x auto) or wrap the tabs.

screen: #/model/transdigm/2025-06-30/forecast ('What drives each case') and .../portfolio-fit ('Where the issuer sits in the portfolio') at 390 px (full)
title: At 390 px the range strips shrink to a blob about 30 px wide between a wrapped label column and the value column, so range and marker positions cannot be read.
expected: D-42 and D-28: a chart stays legible at 390 px or yields to its table form; D-02: a range strip shows markers against a range.
actual: In the Forecast card the strip for each driver is about 30 px wide while the label column wraps to three lines ('Organic revenue / growth / Past five years: -12% to 18%'). The Chart or Table toggle is the only fallback and is not offered by default.
suggested_change: Stack the label above the strip at narrow widths in RangeStripChart (X1 component), or show the table form below 480 px.

screen: #/model/transdigm/2025-06-30/front (info buttons) and .../statements (n.a. and Withheld cells), touch device at 390 px
title: Metric definitions and the reasons behind n.a. and Withheld cells appear only as hover or focus tooltips; a tap on a touch device shows nothing.
expected: D-35: no hover-only information; CM-023: a missing number is 'n.a.' with its reason; CM-022: every figure carries its basis.
actual: MetricTile.tsx:20-27 puts each headline figure's definition in a react-aria Tooltip on a 16 px info button; StatementTable.tsx:54-60 puts a missing or withheld cell's reason in a Tooltip. With a touch context (hasTouch, 390 px) tapping 'About Net leverage' and a cell with a reason produces no [role=tooltip]; with keyboard focus on desktop the same controls show 'Net debt divided by EBITDA as defined' and the reason. The fixture itself carries no cell reasons, so the Statements path was exercised with a copy that adds them.
suggested_change: Show the definition and the reason in a popover that opens on press, or print the reason beside the n.a. as a short line.

title: The Net debt walk table labels a row 'Free cash flow, FY26' with -2,540 while the Statements table shows free cash flow FY26E as +2,540: the same label carries opposite signs.
expected: CM-022 and D-15: every figure carries its label and basis as published; D-14: no figure misdescribed. The chart step for the same row is labelled 'Cash flow FY26', so chart and table name one step differently.
actual: web/fixtures/model.json statements.bridges[1].rows holds 'Free cash flow, FY26' with cells -2,540 and -1,810, and 'Free cash flow, FY27' with -2,836 and -1,870; Statements > Cash flow shows 2,540 and 2,836 for the base case. The values subtract from net debt (26,300 - 2,540 - 2,836 = 20,924, which agrees), so the arithmetic is right and the label carries the net-debt effect, not the cash flow. A reader of the table alone reads negative free cash flow.
suggested_change: Label the rows by their effect ('Effect of free cash flow on net debt, FY26') or use the chart's step label in the table, and state the sign convention in the chart note.

title: The case choice is private state of each page: choosing Downside on Statements leaves Forecast on Base, and leaving a page resets it.
expected: CM-065: forecast cases with 'a shared case choice'; CT-045: choosing a forecast case on the Forecast tab.
actual: StatementsPage.tsx:19 and ForecastPage.tsx:15 each hold `useState(0)`. After choosing Downside on Statements and opening Forecast the Base case is checked; after Portfolio fit and back to Model the choice is Base again.
suggested_change: Hold the chosen case in the run page group (a context beside ShowSources) so both pages and the return from a trace share it.

title: The case-choice line says 'every chart below follows it', but on Statements only the two bridges change and on Forecast only the interest cover line, the walk and a marker emphasis change.
expected: D-16: copy is plain and specific; CM-065 and CT-045: the case choice drives the views it names.
actual: Comparing each card's text before and after choosing Downside: Statements: Bridges (2) change, 'The two cases side by side', Debt by instrument, Maturities by year and Recovery by class and case do not (StatementsPage.tsx:11-15 memoises them on purpose). Forecast: 'EBITDA by case' does not change. The copy on StatementsPage.tsx:27 and ForecastPage.tsx:23 still promises every chart.
suggested_change: Say 'the forecast columns, the bridges and the cash flow walk follow the case; charts that show both cases or the balance sheet date do not' or mark the charts that follow.

title: Only 6 of the 15 chart tables carry a trace control per row; the Headroom, Segment margin, Exposure, Leverage and margin, holdings range, driver, Interest cover, EBITDA by case and cash flow walk tables carry none.
expected: CM-009 and D-06: exactly one labelled trace control per paragraph, row or figure.
actual: Table forms with row controls: EBITDA bridge 6, Net debt walk 6, The two cases side by side 6, Debt by instrument 4, Maturities by year 6, Recovery 3. Zero in the other nine. For Headroom and Segments the code passes `cellRows` with no end cell (AnalysisCharts.tsx:29 and :55) and the slice rows have no trace field; the Forecast walk's rows carry trace null in the fixture although WalkCard supports it. Only the chart-level control reaches those figures.
suggested_change: Add an optional `trace` to the headroom, segment, limits, scatter, strip and path rows and draw it as the other tables do.

title: The static app draws the Model as its own rail area with its own tabs: the statements grid is on the 'Model' tab, not the Forecast page, and the Forecast page is reachable only from the library's Forecast tab.
expected: CM-030: the delivered Model appears as an entry in Modules and on Forecast; CM-064 and CM-116: the model grid is on Forecast (H-05 in output/1-rubrics/harmony-report.md records the conflict).

The Statements, bridges, debt and recovery views live under the 'Model' tab. Whether the Modules entry exists is S3's check.

title: Several chart and content rows the matrix assigns to S5 have no counterpart in the Model group, and its slice type has no field for them: break-point and deleveraging timing, a leverage trend, liquidity and cash runway, sources and uses, value allocation by scenario, yield against maturity.
expected: CM-164, CM-122, CM-124, CM-156, CM-186 to CM-188, CM-176, CM-225, CM-227, CM-321 (D-8 in harmony-report.md maps 'Modules and Forecast run charts' to S5); H-25: check what the fixture holds, not every row.

title: The Limitations page lists every 'Not established for this run' item as a counted set of gap panels, a gap ledger on a page that is not Evidence.

title: Every Model page has the document title 'Credit OS'; the titles written in routes.tsx are never applied to bleed pages.
expected: D-36 and WCAG 2.4.2: a page title that names the page. routes.tsx gives 'Financial models', 'Front page', 'Analysis', 'Model', 'Portfolio fit', 'Limitations' and 'Forecast'.
actual: document.title is 'Credit OS' on every address (web/index.html:13 holds a fixed title). App.tsx:85-91 renders a bleed route without reading `route.title`; the title is used only in the invalid-slice notice. Browser tabs and history list seven pages with one name. The shell is S1's; this lists the S5 addresses.

title: One USD unit is written three ways: '$8,580m' on the Front page, 'USD millions' on Statements and charts, 'US dollars, millions' in the covers list; the matrix asks for 'US$m' for USD.
expected: CM-320: US$m for USD, otherwise the currency code and m (for example GBPm); CM-022: unit, period and basis on every figure.
actual: Front headline tiles show '$8,580m', '$4,560m' and '$1,950m'; Statements headers say 'USD millions unless a unit is shown'; charts say 'USD millions'; Front 'What the model covers' says 'US dollars, millions'. The strings come from the fixture, so the page enforces no single form.
suggested_change: Fix one form in delivery (US$m for USD, code plus m otherwise) and keep it across the tiles, headers and chart subtitles.

title: In the Bars view a negative figure's bar differs from a positive one only by colour: both are right-aligned from the same edge.
expected: D-39: no information carried by colour alone; the figure's own sign is the only other cue.
actual: StatementTable.tsx:94-101 draws every bar with `ml-auto` and chooses `bg-chart-3` for negative and `bg-chart-1` for positive; data-sign is an attribute, not a visible cue. The figure text above keeps its minus sign, so the value is not lost.
suggested_change: Draw negative bars from a centre line or add a pattern.

title: The Forecast page's headings 'Two cases' and 'Cash flow in FY26' are written in the page, not taken from the data, so a walk for another year or a one-case run would carry a wrong heading.
expected: CM-022: period as published; the page adds no wording but the data's.
actual: ForecastPage.tsx:21 and :39 and StatementsPage.tsx:25 hard-code the heading text; the walk's own title and subtitle ('FY26, USD millions') come from the slice. The reader fixes two cases (read.ts:302-303), so 'Two cases' is consistent today; 'FY26' is not tied to any field.
suggested_change: Draw the walk's subtitle period in the section heading.

title: Duplicated markup and unused parts in the Model folder, for the sweep.

title: Chart titles are h3 headings placed after an unrelated h2: Headroom and Segment margins follow 'Measures and what they mean', and the Forecast charts follow 'Two cases'.
expected: D-36: headings in order; an h3 sits under the h2 it belongs to.

Forecast: H2 Two cases, H3 What drives each case, H3 Interest cover, H3 EBITDA by case, H2 Cash flow in FY26. The index lists Headroom and Segment margins as sections of their own. No level is skipped, so this is a structure cue only.
suggested_change: Give Headroom and Segment margins their own h2 (the chart's `as` prop) as the index implies.
